Plastic now accounts for 55 percent of this material, an increase from 47 percent in 2023 and 2025. Consumers report being constrained by the limited packaging choices available in retail settings.

stories.summary: A report from The Revelator suggests that the plastic industry has long promoted recycling to manage public perception of waste. While recycling was presented as a primary solution to pollution, only 9 percent of all plastic ever created has been recycled. The industry remains a central figure.

stories.title: AI-designed packaging faces consumer taste skepticism
stories.summary: A.K. Pradeep of Sensori.ai suggests that while consumers associate AI-designed packaging with health benefits, they remain doubtful regarding the taste of the products inside. The firm is examining how brands might address this perception gap to better align consumer expectations with AI-driven design choices.

The plant offers local businesses an alternative to conventional plastic products, including shopping bags and laundry bags. The company says the materials are designed to biodegrade and compost under suitable conditions.

stories.summary: PureCycle Technologies has secured a multi-year agreement with WM to receive nearly 25 million pounds of waste polypropylene annually. The deal aims to accelerate plastic reuse by pairing WM’s collection scale with PureCycle’s dissolution recycling technology. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in November 2026.

Vitrimers proposed as bridge for thermoset plastic recycling
stories.summary: A comment in the Journal of Materials Science: Composites suggests vitrimers could bridge the recycling gap between thermoplastics and thermosets. Authors Indranil Dey and Suryasarathi Bose argue these polymers, which contain Covalent Adaptable Networks, offer a scalable foundation for circularity in materials that have historically resisted recycling.

stories.title: Dankook researchers use shear force to break down plastic
stories.summary: Researchers at Dankook University have developed a method to break down hard-to-recycle UHMWPE plastic by mixing it with zeolite catalysts and using a twin-screw extruder. The process uses mechanical shear forces to untangle the long molecular chains that typically require high temperatures and energy to process.

stories.title: NEPRA raises Rs 110 crore in first Asian waste-sector equity bet by PIDG
stories.summary: Ahmedabad-based recycler NEPRA has raised Rs 110 crore in equity from the Private Infrastructure Development Group. The investment marks the group's first equity stake in the Asian waste sector. NEPRA plans to use the capital to expand its material recovery facilities and increase plastic recycling capacity.

stories.title: EU bans plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries
stories.summary: The European Union will prohibit plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries starting 21 November 2026. The ban, part of the revised Waste Shipment Regulation, targets the 1 to 1.5 million tonnes of plastic waste the EU exports annually. The Commission says the move promotes responsible waste management.

stories.title: PackUK proposes faster EPR fee increases for red-rated packaging
stories.summary: PackUK has proposed increasing disposal fees for harder-to-recycle packaging to fund discounts for more sustainable alternatives. Under the draft policy, red-rated packaging would face fees twice the base rate in 2027/28, rising to 2.4 times by 2028/29. The current multipliers are 1.6 and 2.0 respectively.

stories.title: Washington fines 38 producers for recycled content shortfalls
stories.summary: Washington regulators fined 38 plastic producers a total of $246,548 for failing to meet minimum postconsumer recycled content requirements in 2025. The Department of Ecology noted that while more companies were penalized this year, the total fine amount decreased as 70 percent of producers achieved compliance.

stories.title: Oregon court conditions EPR fee relief on bond payment
stories.summary: A U.S. District Court judge has granted the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors relief from Oregon’s packaging EPR law pending an appeal. The court conditioned this protection on the association posting a bond equivalent to the fees it would otherwise owe under the state’s recycling mandate.

Study finds plastic alternatives may increase emissions
stories.summary: Replacing single-use polyethylene packaging with paper, glass, aluminium or steel alternatives increased potential greenhouse gas emissions by 190% in the U.S. and 50% in Europe, according to a new life cycle assessment. The substitutions also increased packaging weight by up to sixfold. Physics remains a stubborn variable.

stories.title: Stylam to acquire majority stake in Haripur Kraft
stories.summary: Stylam Industries will acquire a 51% stake in Indian paper producer Haripur Kraft for up to 22.44 crore. The deal, approved on 19 November, leaves existing partners with 24.5% each. Haripur Kraft operates a 125-tonne-a-day plant in Himachal Pradesh. The paper trail now leads to laminates.

stories.title: Silicone coated kraft paper market valued at $4.8 billion
stories.summary: The global market for silicone coated kraft paper enters 2026 valued at approximately $4.8 billion. According to an IndexBox report, the sector is defined by broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The material has evolved to become indispensable in modern manufacturing.

stories.title: Herbs and natural solutions market bifurcates
stories.summary: The global market for herbs and natural solutions is splitting into a high-volume everyday segment and a premium, benefit-specific wellness segment. According to IndexBox, demand is driven by discrete, high-value need states. The industry is moving toward a more disciplined procurement behavior as it enters 2026.

stories.title: Edible pods tested in Northamptonshire
stories.summary: Residents in the hamlet of Nobottle recently trialed edible, biodegradable pods for ginger shots as part of a pilot project with Notpla. Roughly half of the local residents sampled the product. The company aims to address plastic waste, though some residents found the concept unusual.

stories.title: Researchers develop edible packaging from whey
stories.summary: Researchers at GITAM Deemed to be University have developed a prototype for edible, biodegradable food packaging using whey. The project aims to reduce plastic waste while repurposing a nutrient-rich by-product of cheese production that currently contributes to water pollution. The packaging is intended to be consumed.

stories.title: Startup converts chicken feathers into bioplastic
stories.summary: Kanpur-based NovoEarth is converting chicken feathers into biodegradable plastic for agricultural mulch films. The startup extracts keratin from poultry waste at a pilot facility in West Bengal. The company claims the material could boost crop yields by 40%. Poultry waste is finding a second life.

stories.title: Research suggests plastic alternatives raise environmental impact
stories.summary: A study in Resources, Environment and Sustainability found that replacing polyethylene with paper, glass, aluminum or steel can increase global warming potential and water use. Substituting single-use plastic resulted in 190% more greenhouse gas emissions in the U.S. The packaging mass increased by up to six times.

The machine, developed in India, integrates hot-melt technology with a die-cutting unit. It operates at speeds of up to 200 meters per minute, combining global technology with local manufacturing economics.

stories.title: Webtech showcases fifth-generation flexo press
stories.summary: Webtech International Machineries demonstrated its Aeroflex S5 flexographic printing press at Loupe India. The gearless machine features eight servos per print station and an AI-enabled management reporting system. The company claims the automation features improve efficiency by reducing setup time and minimizing material wastage.

stories.title: Koenig and Bauer demonstrate automated postpress
stories.summary: Koenig and Bauer hosted an open house in Milan to demonstrate automated postpress processes. The event addressed industry challenges including short delivery times and a shortage of skilled workers. Over 100 experts attended to view the latest die-cutting and folder-gluer technology at the company's partner showroom.

stories.title: US automatic screw capping market analysis
stories.summary: The U.S. market for automatic screw capping machines is characterized by replacement and upgrade cycles, with equipment lifecycles spanning 10 to 20 years. Indicative pricing for systems ranges from $25,000 to $600,000. Demand is driven by beverage packaging, pharmaceuticals, and food production requirements.

stories.title: German carton sealing market remains mature
stories.summary: The German market for carton sealing machines is driven by replacement demand and labor savings rather than first-time adoption. Equipment lifecycles typically last 8 to 15 years. Demand for belts, tape heads, and glue units remains recurring as operators prioritize throughput and integration needs.

stories.title: Global e-commerce packaging market to top $105 billion by 2031
stories.summary: The global e-commerce packaging market is forecast to grow from $78.4 billion in 2025 to $105.2 billion by 2031. Research from Smithers suggests automation and changing retail models are driving the shift, moving packaging beyond simple protection to an integral part of retail operations.

stories.summary: V-Shapes is rolling out patented snap-and-squeeze packaging to replace traditional tear-off sachets. stories.summary: Shipway has introduced an AI-powered suite to help e-commerce sellers avoid shipping weight discrepancies and unexpected charges.
